description: Figure 9 is a composite of three panel types. (a) is a 2x3 EPMA montage: top row SEI (secondary-electron image, 20 µm scale bar), Fe map (orange, uniform), Mn map (bright green, uniform); bottom row COMPO (backscattered/composite image, 20 µm scale bar), Al map (green, uniform), C map (blue, uniform). Each colour map has a vertical blue-to-red intensity scale but no printed numbers; all six panels show the same equiaxed grain structure with occasional annealing twins and no pronounced segregation. (b) is an engineering stress–strain curve (x: Engineering strain/%, ticks 0-40; y: Engineering stress/MPa, ticks 0-1200 in steps of 200) for the condition labelled "Fe-30Mn-8Al-1C : 1000°C/15min-550°C/2h"; the single red curve rises steeply to a plateau at the 1000 MPa gridline, then increases gradually to a maximum just above the 1100 MPa gridline near 40% strain before a sharp fracture drop. (c) is an optical micrograph with a 50 µm scale bar showing equiaxed grains with straight annealing twins and no second phase. Together the panels argue that uniformly distributed Fe/Mn/Al/C in a single-phase austenitic matrix yields a steel combining high strength with large ductility. The second supplied image is a magnified duplicate of (b).
measured_quantities: element distribution of Fe, Mn, Al, C (map intensity, a.u.)

observations.observation: Panel (a) contains two greyscale electron images (SEI and COMPO) and four colour element maps labelled Fe, Mn, Al and C, all acquired over the same field of view.
The SEI and COMPO panels in (a) each carry a 20 µm scale bar; panel (c) carries a 50 µm scale bar.
The Fe, Mn, Al and C maps in (a) are homogeneous, with no banding or segregation contrast, and each has a blue-to-red vertical intensity bar on which no numeric values are printed.
Panel (b) plots Engineering stress/MPa versus Engineering strain/% with y ticks at 0, 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000, 1200 and x ticks at 0, 10, 20, 30, 40.
The legend of panel (b) reads 'Fe-30Mn-8Al-1C : 1000°C/15min-550°C/2h', identifying the sample and its processing condition.

The stress-strain curve in (b) shows a very short elastic/transition region, a plateau near the 1000 MPa gridline, gradual hardening to a maximum just above the 1100 MPa gridline close to 40% strain, followed by an abrupt load drop.
No numeric strength or elongation values are printed on the curve in (b); the values must be read from the gridlines.
The optical micrograph (c) shows equiaxed grains containing straight, parallel annealing twins typical of a single austenitic (FCC) phase, with no second-phase particles.
The caption states panel (a) comprises secondary electron and backscattered electron maps, panel (b) engineering stress-strain curves, and panel (c) optical micrographs.
The citing text states the EPMA maps reveal uniform distribution of all steel elements (Fe, Mn, Al, C) and confirm a single FCC phase.
The citing text reports yield strength of 953 MPa, tensile strength of 1109 MPa and elongation of 42% for the alloy; these numbers are not printed anywhere on the figure itself.
The citing text concludes that the austenitic low-density steel combines high strength with excellent ductility, which is the argument the figure supports.

subfigures.description: 2x3 EPMA montage. Top row: SEI secondary-electron image (20 µm scale bar) showing equiaxed grains with annealing twins; Fe map (orange, homogeneous); Mn map (bright green, homogeneous). Bottom row: COMPO backscattered/composite image (20 µm scale bar) with the same grain structure; Al map (green, homogeneous); C map (blue, homogeneous). Every colour map has a vertical blue(low)-to-red(high) scale bar with no printed numeric values.

Engineering stress-strain curve, x-axis Engineering strain/% (ticks 0-40), y-axis Engineering stress/MPa (ticks 0-1200). Single red curve, legend 'Fe-30Mn-8Al-1C : 1000°C/15min-550°C/2h'. Curve jumps steeply to a ~1000 MPa plateau, hardens gradually to a maximum just above the 1100 MPa gridline at ~40% strain, then drops sharply (fracture/necking) to below 1000 MPa.
A second, magnified copy of panel (b) supplied in the same group; identical axes, legend and curve shape, no additional data.
Optical micrograph with 50 µm scale bar showing equiaxed single-phase grains with numerous straight, parallel annealing twins; no second phase or precipitate contrast visible.

unreadable_items: panel (a): the vertical colour-scale bars for the Fe, Mn, Al and C maps carry no printed numeric values, so the intensity range cannot be quantified
panel (b): the exact strain and stress at the maximum and at fracture are not printed and can only be bracketed between gridlines
the second supplied image is a magnified copy of panel (b) and contributes no new information
